claims.statement: The personal-instruction fragment is an HTML support label only; it supplies no scope, precedence, authorization or proof of effective runtime application.
The repository-wide instruction label names .github/copilot-instructions.md. Presence of that file is distinct from its being loaded, applying to the relevant product surface or enforcing behavior.

The close-session fragment distinguishes running sessions, which are ended and saved before sidebar removal, from nonrunning sessions, which are removed from the sidebar. Removal is not irreversible deletion: resuming through the session picker can display a removed session again.

The pinned cloud-agent limitation excludes personal repositories owned by managed users because hosted runners are unavailable for those personal repositories. It is not a blanket exclusion of managed-user enterprise organization repositories.

The required-host fragment lists uploads.github.com and user-images.githubusercontent.com and separates individual, business and enterprise Copilot API hosts by the expected users' plan. It is a fragment of requirements, not a complete network security specification or permission to expand an allowlist.

The host fragment additionally lists npmjs.org, npmjs.com, registry.npmjs.com, registry.npmjs.org and skimdb.npmjs.com when using the Codex third-party coding agent. This conditional dependency must not be imposed on every agent or treated as a supply-chain trust certificate.

The validation introduction says the cloud agent by default performs security checks and seeks a Copilot code-review second opinion, attempting resolution before completing a pull request. Attempts and intended risk reduction do not guarantee vulnerability absence, independent review or successful remediation on any actual pull request.
